tfn.s: The writer suggests that a crowd can make a restaurant look better than the food alone would.

tfn.s: The text implies that a customer who waits only briefly is likely to be disappointed.

speak.title: Role-play: the famous queue
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: the friend who wants to go
a.text: You've seen a famous food stall online. The queue is very long and some people wait all night. Ask your friend to come with you. Explain why you want to go and how you'll make the wait easier.

b.text: Your friend wants to wait a very long time for a famous snack. You think it's too much. Ask at least two questions, then say yes, say no, or suggest a different plan.

phrases: I'd love to try it, it's all over my feed.
Isn't it a bit silly to wait that long for a potato?
We could go on a weekday, when it's quieter.
I don't mind queuing if we take chairs and snacks.
That's a lot of time for one meal.
Let's compromise: we'll wait two hours, not twenty-four.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did your friend agree to go, and was the plan fair?
